title: Tenant dependency shepherd and tiered venting policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a per-entity (dependency/model/tenant) 'shepherd' that applies tiered venting (controlled shedding) and safe fallbacks when upstream dependency health or SLO drift is detected. The feature should: 1) synthesize SLO-aligned trip thresholds per entity, 2) provide a staged venting policy (soft shed -> aggressive shed -> circuit open), 3) select safe fallback model/route with semantic degradation guarantees, and 4) integrate with multi-region failover and per-tenant priority. Goal: reduce cascading overloads and preserve response surface for high-priority tenants while meeting SLOs for critical routes.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant/per-model/per-dependency breaker configured and active in runtime for >= 90% of production traffic in canary region
Tiered venting rules trigger in simulation for injected load and degrade according to policy (soft->hard->open) with expected token-cost reductions
Automatic selection of fallback route/model returns responses within verified semantic bounds (precision/recall baselines) for >95% of fallbacks in test corpus
Dashboards show clear metrics: breaker state, venting level, failover count, and per-tenant latency/cost impact
Runbook includes manual overrides, safehold mode, and rollback steps and has been validated in tabletop exercise
implementation_notes: Shepherd concept: lightweight controller per dependency that consumes runtime telemetry (p99/p95 latency, error rate, queue depth, tokens/sec) and computes a score to decide vent level

Venting levels: 0=normal, 1=soft (request shaping, prefix caching unlocks, reduce max_tokens), 2=hard (reject low-priority classes, degrade model to quantized/cheaper variant), 3=open (route to fallback or reject with clear retry-after)

Trip thresholds: combine fixed thresholds and adaptive windows. Initial thresholds: p99_latency_ms > 1200 OR error_rate_1m > 2% triggers level 1; sustained for 30s escalates to level 2; further breach escalates to level 3. Use hysteresis windows to avoid flapping
Tenant priority: tenants have priority tiers (critical, standard, dev). Venting policy reduces lowest-priority traffic first. Priority mapping stored in tenant config service and cached by runtime
Fallback selection: prefer model variant with same output schema and previously evaluated on regression suite. If unavailable, route to remote-region endpoint with capacity-aware tagging
Safety guarantees: preservation of structured output shapes and consistent status codes for clients using function-calling or structured outputs
Integration: hook into routing policy engine for cross-region failover; use circuit state protocol published to control-plane for console visibility
telemetry_metrics: shed_rate (requests rejected or downgraded) per tenant
rollout_plan: Design and unit tests (week 1-2): build shepherd controller and local simulator
Canary: enable for internal tenants and infra routes in eu-west-1 only (week 3)
Production staged: roll to additional regions with metric gates (p99 latency and error rate budgets) during week 4-6
Full rollout: enable per-customer priority mapping and tenant-specific configs (week 7)
Post-rollout: continuous calibration for thresholds using historical traffic profiles and automated A/B experiments
tests: Synthetic spike tests: ramp qps by 5x to verify venting levels and no downstream outage
Chaos: inject latency into dependency V to confirm graceful fallback and routing to alternate region
Regression: fallback model must pass prompt-compatibility tests (structure + top-3 intent match) on benchmark corpus
Load-shedding correctness: verify dev tenants are first to be shed and critical tenants maintain >90% success rate
Stress soak: 24-hour soak with varied request shapes to validate hysteresis and no flapping
